key_insight: Deep learning models can screen pediatric sleep apnea from multichannel EEG, with the best performance coming from a vision transformer trained on topological data analysis features.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EEG-based automated apnea screening could reduce manual polysomnography workload, but performance is still modest and variable across patient groups.
method: Compared Vision Transformers and Graph Attention Networks.
Tested multiple EEG representations: raw signals, spectrograms, coherence graphs, and TDA-derived features.
Used age- and sex-matched pediatric train/test splits.
evidence_signal: Trained on 2,410 pediatric subjects and tested on 575, with the best test AUC reaching 0.750.
watch_item: Performance varied notably by demographics and sleep stage, so clinical deployment would require careful validation across subgroups.
paper_title: Deep Learning Approaches for Sleep Apnea Classification from Polysomnographic EEG Signals
